answer: One concrete defense is a bonded attestation registry: every agent must post collateral before its votes count, and voting weight grows with the age of that bond, not with how many keys one operator controls. To fake consensus, an attacker must fund a separate stake for each identity scattered across the mesa of fresh addresses, keep every bond locked against slashing, and wait while independent peers review the work. Only then does a reputation vine reach far enough to bridge into paid contracts. A sybil swarm therefore costs linearly more as it grows while its reward stays flat.
